subject: Operator activity export: time-bounded deltas, redaction rules, retrieval SLAs
messages:
From: AuditOps (audits@goldcrest.com)
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: compliance@goldcresthealth.com
Date: 2028-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: operator activity slice for SIG & CAIQ review

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the intro — we need a narrow, time-bounded extract of operator/admin activity to support Goldcrest's SIG/CAIQ review. Goal is minimal exposure: start/end window + delta changes (only events that changed state) over a 72-hour incident window. Primary asks: 1) what fields are exported (actor, action, resource, timestamp, before/after where applicable), 2) redaction policy for PII in args/metadata, and 3) expected retrieval SLA for ad hoc pulls (hours/minutes).

Ideally we can get a sample manifest and a 24–48 hour slice within the week. Attachment: none.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
AuditOps, Goldcrest Health
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: AuditOps (audits@goldcrest.com)
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator activity slice for SIG & CAIQ review

Maya / Goldcrest team —

Thanks for the clear ask. We can produce a time-bounded delta export for operator/admin events. Quick summary up-front:
- Export fields: actor (internal id + email), action type, resource path, timestamp (ISO8601 UTC), request_id, event_payload (subject to redaction), before_state / after_state (for config changes).
- Redaction: configurable per-request using a redaction matrix; default is to mask long fields (>= 200 chars) and remove keys flagged as pii in our manifest.
- SLA: for on-demand slices under 72 hours we can commit to 6 hours retrieval; for larger/archival pulls we provide an ETA with a signed manifest (usually 24–48 hours).

Cc'ing Kim and Vivek to confirm the export format and attachments. We'll produce a sample CSV manifest and a redaction matrix.

Next steps:
1) Kim: can you confirm the export schema and sample file?
2) Maya: can you confirm the exact UTC window you want and whether Goldcrest prefers masking vs full removal for user identifiers in payloads?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2028-07-01T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: operator activity slice for SIG & CAIQ review

Jordan / team —

Attaching a sample export manifest and a draft redaction matrix. Key implementation notes (technical):

- Format: CSV (UTF-8) for tabular delivery; each row = single event. Fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, actor_type (operator/service), actor_email_hash, action, resource, request_id, before_json_base64 (nullable), after_json_base64 (nullable), metadata_kv (json-string).
- Delta logic: we compute diffs server-side for resource mutations and populate before/after; read-only events have before_json_base64 empty.
- Redaction rules: we provide three tiers: none, mask, remove. For compliance reviews we recommend mask for user identifiers and remove for secrets/keys. The attached sample-redaction-matrix.xlsx maps JSON keys to tiers.
- PII in free-form args: we run a best-effort pattern matcher that flags emails, SSNs, phone numbers. Matches are handled per-requesting party preference; we log redaction decisions in operator-delta-manifest.csv (redaction_reason column).
- Transport: SFTP or signed HTTPS bundle (we prefer HTTPS + pre-signed expiring URL).
- Integrity: signed manifest with SHA256 checksums and a short audit trail (extraction_user, extraction_started_at, extraction_completed_at).

Attachments in this thread: operator-delta-manifest.csv (sample), sample-redaction-matrix.xlsx

If Goldcrest needs the payloads fully anonymized (no email_hashes or actor identifiers), that requires an entitlement and contract amendment; otherwise we can hash actor emails (salted) with the provided salt per-request.

Kimberly Park
Product Security (Compliance Integrations) | Redwood Inference

Maya —

Following up: we uploaded a 48-hour sample slice for your review (link below) and included the manifest with redaction_reason annotations. Summary of what you'll find: salted actor_email_hash (masking option applied), before/after for all config changes, and a redaction column explaining any removed payload keys. Retrieval was performed via signed HTTPS URL (valid 72 hours).

Link: https://s3.redwoodinference.com/exports/GC-2028-0042/sample-48h-delta.csv (signed link sent to audits@goldcrest.com)

If this looks good, confirm whether Goldcrest wants:
A) masked/hashes retained (default), or
B) full anonymization (requires contract amendment), or
C) include actor mapping via an NDA + KMS-wrapped salt exchange.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call to walk the sample.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
